descriptionChirho: The core Christian theological concept of selfless, unconditional love — whether God's love for humanity, human love for God, or mutual love among believers; the dominant NT ethical term encompassing both the divine attribute and the commanded human response. All major translations use their primary word for deep affective love: Spanish amor, Arabic مَحَبَّة (mahabbah), Korean 사랑 (sarang), Hindi प्रेम (prem), Swahili upendo. This is the word Paul personifies in 1 Corinthians 13 and that John declares is God's very nature (1 John 4:8).

A specific early-church communal meal, the agape feast, referenced in Jude 12 (and paralleled in 2 Peter 2:13) where false teachers are described as blemishes at these gatherings; distinct from the abstract virtue because it denotes a concrete social-liturgical event. Spanish renders it fiestas-de-amor, Hindi प्रेम-भोजों-में ('in love-meals'), Arabic ولائم-محبة (wala'im mahabbah, 'love banquets'), Korean 사랑의-잔치에서 ('at love feasts'), Swahili karamu-za-upendo ('love feasts'). The dative plural form (ἀγάπαις) confirms the concrete-event reading.
